nodes.summary: Natural numbers $p$ and $q$ are consecutive primes when $p$ and $q$ are prime, $p < q$, and every prime $r$ satisfies $r \le p$ or $q \le r$; that is, no prime lies strictly between $p$ and $q$.
nodes.title: Consecutive primes

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 = 2$, $p_1 = 3$, $p_2 = 5, \dots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the prime gap at $n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $n$ with $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 6 (increasing prime gaps)

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $p_n$ and $p_{n+1}$ are consecutive primes: both are prime, $p_n < p_{n+1}$, and no prime lies strictly between them.
nodes.title: Successive primes in the enumeration are consecutive

nodes.summary: The proposition that Vardi's prime-gap asymptotic does not hold.
nodes.title: Negation of Vardi's prime-gap asymptotic

nodes.summary: A list $l$ of natural numbers is a block of consecutive primes when $l$ is nonempty, every entry of $l$ is prime, $l$ is strictly increasing, and every two adjacent entries of $l$ are consecutive primes.
nodes.title: Block of consecutive primes

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a predicate on natural numbers. A list $l$ of natural numbers is a block of consecutive primes restricted by $P$ when $l$ is a block of consecutive primes and every entry of $l$ satisfies $P$.
nodes.title: Restricted block of consecutive primes

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 = 2 < p_1 = 3 < p_2 = 5 < \dots$ be the primes in increasing order, let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function, and for real $x$ let $d(x)$ be the largest prime gap $p_{n+1} - p_n$ over all $n$ with $p_n < x$, with $d(x) = 0$ when no prime is less than $x$. For a real number $C$, this is the function on pairs $(x, y)$ of real numbers given by $\pi(\lfloor y + C\,d(x) \rfloor) - \pi(\lfloor y \rfloor)$, where…
nodes.title: Primes in a window of $C$ maximal prime gaps

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $g_n = 2$ if and only if $p_n + 2$ is prime.
nodes.title: A prime gap equals two exactly at a twin prime

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n = 2$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, if and only if there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2$ is also prime.
nodes.title: The liminf of prime gaps is two exactly when there are infinitely many twin primes

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order, let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap, and let $L = \liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. For every natural number $B$, $L \le B$ if and only if $g_n \le B$ for infinitely many $n$.
nodes.title: When the liminf of prime gaps is at most a given bound

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order, let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap, and let $L = \liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$. Then $L \ne \infty$ if and only if there is a natural number $B > 0$ such that infinitely many primes $p$ admit a prime $q$ with $p < q$ and $q - p \le B$.
nodes.title: Finite liminf of prime gaps and bounded gaps between primes

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. The liminf of prime gaps is $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; the value $\infty$ is allowed.
nodes.title: Liminf of prime gaps

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $g_n > 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, including $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Prime gaps are positive

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 = 2$, $p_1 = 3$, $p_2 = 5, \dots$ be the primes in increasing order, indexed from $0$. For a natural number $n$, the prime gap at $n$ is $p_{n+1} - p_n$.
nodes.title: Prime gap

nodes.summary: The filter on pairs $(x, y)$ of real numbers along which $x \to \infty$ while $x/2 < y < x$: a set of pairs belongs to it exactly when it contains every pair $(x, y)$ with $x/2 < y < x$ and $x$ sufficiently large.
nodes.title: The regime $x \to \infty$ with $x/2 < y < x$

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 = 2 < p_1 = 3 < p_2 = 5 < \dots$ be the primes in increasing order. For a real number $x$, $d(x)$ is the largest prime gap $p_{n+1} - p_n$ over all $n$ with $p_n < x$ (the next prime $p_{n+1}$ may exceed $x$), and $d(x) = 0$ when no prime is less than $x$.
nodes.title: Largest prime gap below $x$

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. Then $\liminf_{n \to \infty} g_n \ge 2$, where the liminf is taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: The liminf of prime gaps is at least two

nodes.summary: Let $p_0 < p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes in increasing order and let $g_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$ be the $n$-th prime gap. For every $n \ge 1$, $g_n \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Prime gaps after the first are at least two

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be the prime-counting function and, for real $x$, let $d(x)$ be the largest prime gap $p_{n+1} - p_n$ over the primes $p_n < x$. It is not true that for every real $C > 1$, $\pi(\lfloor y + C\,d(x) \rfloor) - \pi(\lfloor y \rfloor)$ is asymptotically equivalent to $C\,d(x) / \log y$ as $x \to \infty$ over pairs $(x, y)$ with $x/2 < y < x$.
nodes.title: Vardi's prime-gap asymptotic is false

nodes.title: Vardi's prime-gap asymptotic
